Subject: Multipath routing carveout request for CuraHealth pilot — no-fallback window

Laura / Marissa,

Quick context: CuraHealth (pilot) needs a short-lived routing exception for their production pilot next week. Their regulatory team requires that all inference for a specific tenant run against a single model variant hosted in the US region and that no automatic fallback be used for the first 72 hours after go-live. They are asking us to: enforce region lock (us-east), force model variant v3-quant-8b, and disable fallback to cheaper/approximate variants during the 72-hour acceptance window.

Why they ask: their downstream audit checks correlate token-level outputs against a certified model fingerprint. Any automatic fallback or routing to a different variant would break their compliance attestation.

What I'm asking from Product/Ops:
- Decision on whether we can temporarily disable automatic fallback for a single tenant + model for 72 hours (no-global impact).
- If yes, an ops runbook for safe rollback and metrics to monitor (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta).
- Any blockers from infra (batching/caching assumptions), and expected performance hit estimate.

Attachments: CuraHealth_Multipath_Req.pdf (customer-signed scope), fallback-risk-mitigation.xlsx (initial risk proposals).

Proposed timeline: approval by EOD Wed (8/19) so we can schedule a limited deploy on Thu (8/20).

Customer note: Sam is on this thread and can approve the timebox on their side.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the write-up and attachments. High level thoughts from Product:

1) Policy model: We can scope a routing policy to a tenant + model version for a limited time, but there are two concerns:
   - Caching & KV assumptions: our prefix caching can serve stale keys if we forcibly pin the model without clearing caches. We need a cache invalidation step as part of deploy.
   - Autoscaling/throughput: forcing a single heavier variant will increase cost and likely increase latency. We should estimate headroom for the tenant pool.

2) No-fallback implications:
   - If we disable fallback and the forced variant experiences OOMs or kernel failures, requests will error rather than degrade to a lighter model. That will cause immediate customer-visible failures.

3) Proposed safeguards before we agree:
   - Timebox: 72h max as requested, with automated rollback if error-rate > 1% or p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for more than 15 minutes.
   - Canary: route 10% of production traffic to the pinned variant for 2 hours prior to full switch (with fallback enabled during canary).
   - Ops play: pre-warm KV cache, increase headroom on the node pool, and schedule on-call from infra during the window.

If Ops/SRE can confirm the cache invalidation step and a rollback hook, I can sign off from Product.

-Laura

Adding customer context and acceptance constraints from my side:

- CuraHealth is willing to accept the risk of a hard error rather than a fallback if that preserves their audit chain; they will hold the pilot to off-hours traffic (we agreed to a late-night window) to minimize end-user impact.
- Legal asked for a short amendment to our data-processing addendum — they can sign a 72-hour waiver.
- They are asking for two operational guarantees: 1) a documented rollback plan we can run in < 10 minutes, and 2) a single point-of-contact on our side during the 72h.

On SLA: they asked whether we can ensure no SLA credits if the hard error path is taken and they caused the request pattern (they will accept that as long as we document it). I flagged this to revenue but we need Product/Legal confirmation.

From CS perspective, timeline is tight but doable if Product/Ops can confirm the canary + rollback automation by EOD Wed.
